stem.en: A mango tree must carry water and minerals from its roots to its leaves, and carry food to all its parts. Which arrangement shows division of labour?

text.en: Every cell of the tree passes along a little water and a little food, whichever reaches it first.

feedback.en: Here every cell does both jobs, so the work is not divided. This is the plan where every cell does everything.

text.en: One tissue, xylem, carries water and minerals; another tissue, phloem, carries food.
Phloem carries water and minerals, and xylem carries the food, so both jobs are covered.

feedback.en: The jobs are divided, but the wrong way round. Xylem carries water and minerals, and phloem carries food.

text.en: One tissue carries water, minerals and food together, so the tree needs only one kind of tube.

feedback.en: One tissue doing both jobs is not division of labour. Plants have two different conducting tissues.

explanation.en: In plants, the conducting tissues share out the work of transport. Xylem carries water and minerals, while phloem carries food. Each is a group of cells that does its own job.

hints.en: Recall the two conducting tissues of plants and what each one carries.
